subject: Cache telemetry rollout + alerting approval (prefix/KV cache metrics)
body:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 9:12 AM PDT
Subject: Cache telemetry rollout + alerting approval (prefix/KV cache metrics)

Ava — looking for final approval to proceed with prod rollout this week for the new prefix/KV cache telemetry + initial guardrail alerts.

What’s ready:
- Runtime flags + sampling controls merged (default OFF in prod): https://github.com/redwoodinference/redwood/pull/18429
- Dashboards + initial alert rules merged into observability pack:
  - Dashboard panels: https://github.com/redwoodinference/observability-pack/pull/612
  - Ingestion cardinality guards: https://github.com/redwoodinference/observability-pack/pull/613
- Perf canary gating PR (measures p95/p99 overhead): https://github.com/redwoodinference/perf-canary/pull/287

Links you may want:
- Runbook (pipeline/metrics drop + mitigation): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PLAT/Cache+telemetry+pipeline+incident+runbook
- Dashboard spec (what we’re showing + breakdowns): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PLAT/Cache+hit-rate+dashboards+spec
- Grafana (prod-ready dashboards, currently pointing at staging datasets):
  - Cache telemetry overview: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/cache-telemetry/cache-telemetry-overview
  - Regressions triage view: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/cache-telemetry/cache-telemetry-regressions

Proposed rollout plan (high level):
1) Tue AM: enable metrics in staging + validate join keys (route/model/version/region) and sampling.
2) Tue PM: perf-canary gate must remain green (no >0.7% p95 regression; no alloc spikes).
3) Wed: canary prod enable (1% of traffic, Hosted only) for 4 hours.
4) Thu: ramp to 10% Hosted + 1 Dedicated cell (opt-in) if alerts are quiet and cardinality cost is within budget.

Alert policy proposal (guardrails, not customer-facing SLO):
- Page only on: (a) telemetry drop/dashboards flatline; (b) severe hit-rate collapse correlated with eviction pressure across multiple models/regions.
- Otherwise create ticket (hit-rate drift likely workload-mix).

If you’re good with the above, I’ll mark as approved and have Release run the enablement + comms.

Attachments:
- cache-telemetry-rollout-gates-v3.pdf (application/pdf)
- perf-canary-cache-telemetry-overhead-20250309.png (image/png)

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
VP Engineering, Platform & Telemetry
Redwood Inference


From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 10:03 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Cache telemetry rollout + alerting approval (prefix/KV cache metrics)

Thanks. Two questions before I sign off:

1) What’s the rollback trigger / rollback mechanism if we see unexpected cardinality cost or overhead?
2) Confirm we’re not paging on expected diurnal/workload-mix shifts (I don’t want oncall getting hammered for normal variance).

Also: please ensure the runbook includes “how to tell telemetry missing vs real regression” as step 1.

— Ava
Ava Chen
CTO
Redwood Inference


From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 11:21 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Cache telemetry rollout + alerting approval (prefix/KV cache metrics)

All fair.

1) Rollback triggers + mechanism
- Trigger A (overhead): perf-canary red OR prod canary p95 +0.7% sustained for 15m (same workload window), or p99 +1.0% sustained for 15m.
- Trigger B (cardinality/cost): ingestion-side “label-drop rate” >2% OR cache telemetry series count >1.2x projected for >30m.
- Mechanism:
  - Immediate: flip the runtime feature flags off (config hot-reload) for cache metrics emit.
  - Also: ingestion guards will drop forbidden labels by default (so worst case we lose granularity, not explode series count).
  - Dashboards/alerts are safe to leave in place; they’ll just go quiet.

2) Paging policy / avoid paging on workload mix
- Alerts are scoped to multi-signal + multi-dimension conditions:
  - For “cache hit-rate collapse” we require: hit-rate down + eviction pressure up + wasted prefill up, and it must affect >1 model family or >1 region.
  - Otherwise it’s a ticket (route/model-specific or workload-driven).
- We also set a “telemetry validity” panel (metric ingestion health + label-drop) that is checked before interpreting hit-rate.

Runbook update: agree — we already have the first section as “Telemetry missing vs. real regression” (symptom checklist + queries). I’ll add an explicit step 1 call-out + link it from the dashboard.

If you want, I can also hard-cap canary at 1% until we confirm series counts within budget.

— Priya


From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 12:07 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Cache telemetry rollout + alerting approval (prefix/KV cache metrics)

Approved with two conditions:

- Keep prod at 1% for at least 4 hours and explicitly confirm:
  (a) perf-canary still green, (b) label-drop < 1%, (c) series count within plan.
- Please post a short go/no-go note to the leadership channel after the 1% window (one paragraph + links).

Otherwise go ahead.

— Ava


From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 3:47 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Cache telemetry rollout + alerting approval (prefix/KV cache metrics)

Sounds good — we’ll hold at 1% for 4h and treat those three checks as hard gates.

I’ll:
- Update the rollout PDF with the 1% hold gate + thresholds.
- Add the explicit step-1 callout in the runbook (“telemetry missing vs real regression”).
- Post go/no-go summary w/ Grafana links after the window.

Thanks.

— Priya
